We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have identified possible disconnections:

- The sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings: could be formed by sulfonyl chloride + aniline. Template 733 shows sulfonamide formation from aryl sulfonyl chloride and aniline.

- The amide side chain: C=CC(=O)N attached to phenyl (aniline). Could be formed by coupling of an acid chloride (or activated acid) with aniline. Template 891549 shows amide formation from acid chloride and aniline? Actually retro: product is C=CC(=O)N-aryl; retro suggests cleavage to acid chloride (CH3-O-CO?) Wait template 891549: retro smarts: [CH2]=[CH]-C(=O)-NH-aryl -> [CH3]-C-O-C(=O)-CH3 (acid chloride?) Actually mapping: product to precursors: acid chloride (CH3-C(O)-Cl?) plus aniline. The template shows conversion to [CH3]-C-O-[C]=O (maybe acid chloride) and aniline. So we can use commercially available 4-iodo? Actually we need C=CC(=O)N-aryl (anilide). Precursors: aniline (c3ccccc3N) and acryloyl chloride (CH2=CH-COCl). Acryloyl chloride is commercially available? Likely yes. Check buyable: "C=CC(=O)Cl". Let's test is_buyable.
